# Evolving text with GEPA

Walk through candidate selection, reflective mutation and merging, one step at a time. Evolve a short triage prompt with the hosted model, kept cheap by a small dataset, recorded replies and at most three live refinements.

**[▶ Take this lab on the Zenable Learning Hub](https://www.zenable.app/learn?lab=gepa-prompt-evolution&utm_source=github&utm_medium=labs_repo&utm_campaign=gepa-prompt-evolution_readme)** — fully hosted sandbox environment, progress tracking, and a full-featured lab workspace.

Eligible paid Zenable customers get an OpenRouter key automatically in their sandbox. Take the hosted version of this lab, with the key already configured, at https://www.zenable.app/learn?lab=gepa-prompt-evolution&utm_source=github&utm_medium=labs_repo&utm_campaign=gepa-prompt-evolution_readme.

**Duration** 60 minutes · **Difficulty** Advanced

**Topics** `How LLMs Work` · `Verification`

**Prerequisites**

- Comfort reading Python and a shell prompt
- Optional OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key for live runs off the sandbox

---

_This README is only the hands-on lab. The concept walk-through (Overview) lives on the [Learning Hub](https://www.zenable.app/learn?lab=gepa-prompt-evolution&utm_source=github&utm_medium=labs_repo&utm_campaign=gepa-prompt-evolution_readme)._

## Set up AI inference

Your sandbox has no hosted AI key. Automatic keys require an eligible paid plan and an available inference budget. Choose your own OpenRouter key, or use the local model and the lab's recorded-answer steps.

### Option A: use your own OpenRouter key

Create a key at [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys). Then run this in the sandbox terminal, with your key in place of `sk-or-...`:

```bash
zenable-configure-inference sk-or-...
```

The command writes your key and the model settings into `~/.env` and configures every coding agent installed on the sandbox. Open a new terminal so your shell picks them up.

> [!WARNING]
> Your key goes in `~/.env`, never in the lab directory. Every attendee in the sandbox network can read the lab remote, and a key committed there is a key you've shared.

### Option B: use local Ollama (no key)

The sandbox runs [Ollama](https://ollama.com/) with a small model, `qwen3-nothink`, already downloaded and built. Point every agent at it:

```bash
zenable-configure-inference --ollama
```

Then open a new terminal. The model runs on the sandbox's CPU, so expect slower and weaker answers than a hosted model gives you. This option configures coding agents only. For steps that call Jev directly, follow the lab's recorded-answer instructions, such as adding `--fixtures` where shown. Those commands do not switch to recordings automatically.

<details>
<summary>Not on a Zenable sandbox?</summary>

For Option B, install Ollama from [ollama.com/download](https://ollama.com/download). `qwen3:1.7b` is a reasoning model, and thinking makes it very slow on a CPU, so the steps below build a copy with thinking turned off.

Download the model. Run this on its own and wait for it to finish, because the progress display takes over the terminal and swallows anything you paste behind it:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3:1.7b
```

Then build a copy of it with thinking pinned off. It reuses the weights already on disk, so there's no download and it finishes in about a second:

```bash
ollama show --modelfile qwen3:1.7b > Modelfile.nothink
sed -i 's|^FROM /.*|FROM qwen3:1.7b|' Modelfile.nothink
sed -i 's|{{- if and $.IsThinkSet (eq $i $lastUserIdx) }}|{{- if (eq $i $lastUserIdx) }}|' Modelfile.nothink
sed -i 's|{{- if $.Think -}}|{{- if false -}}|' Modelfile.nothink
sed -i 's|{{ if and $.IsThinkSet (not $.Think) -}}|{{ if true -}}|' Modelfile.nothink
grep -q '{{ if true -}}' Modelfile.nothink
ollama create qwen3-nothink -f Modelfile.nothink
```

Then set the variables below in your environment, for example in a `~/.env` file that your shell loads with `set -a; . ~/.env; set +a`. Claude Code reads the `ANTHROPIC_*` variables, and agents that speak the OpenAI API, such as Codex, read `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

For Option A, with your OpenRouter key in place of `sk-or-...`:

```text
ZENABLE_SANDBOX_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-or-...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5
TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api
TYPESAFE_API_KEY=sk-or-...
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-or-...
```

For Option B:

```text
ZENABLE_SANDBOX_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=qwen3-nothink
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
OPENAI_API_KEY=ollama
```

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` stays empty on purpose: Claude Code prefers it over `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` when it holds a value.

</details>

## Getting started

_~5 min · Hands-on_

Let's get the repository and its pinned dependencies:

```bash
cd ~
git clone https://github.com/Zenable-io/labs.git ~/zenable-labs 2>/dev/null \
  || git -C ~/zenable-labs pull --ff-only
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv sync --locked
```

The sandbox comes pre-configured with a model to be used for scoring and reflection.

## Genetic Optimization

_~8 min · Hands-on_

**Candidates → selection → mutations → candidates.**

Let's start with one candidate and measure it. A correct label scores 1; a miss scores 0.

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab baseline --misses 2
```

```console
scoring with openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

prompt:
  Classify this log line as page, ticket, or ignore.

exact-match score by split
  train        70.0%  (20 lines)
  validation   66.7%  (12 lines)
  held-out     50.0%  (8 lines)

14 lines are still wrong, the first 2:
  CRITICAL staging db-primary replication halted, replica lag 1840s and climbing
    expected ignore, answered page: Staging never reaches on-call; the staging owners watch their own dashboard.
  ERROR canary checkout-api 503 on 40% of canary requests, canary auto-rolled back
    expected ignore, answered page: Canary failures roll themselves back and never reach on-call.

40 model calls
```

The seed gets the obvious lines. Look at the missed lines: each one comes with the reason behind its label, and that reason is what reflection reads. Each mutation will propose a new prompt, then we'll measure it again.

## Pareto-Optimal Candidate Selection

_~10 min · Hands-on_

Let's score three prepared candidates. One adds definitions of the three labels; another adds rules for the lines a definition alone gets wrong.

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab select --seed 0
```

```console
scoring with openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

Validation scores for three prepared candidates:
  seed          66.7%  dominated
  definitions   75.0%  available for sampling
  rules         83.3%  available for sampling

Sampled parent: definitions

A line definitions gets right and rules misses:
  ERROR mailer SMTP timeout sending receipt 8821; resent on attempt 2, delivered

36 model calls
```

Compare the two averages, then look at the last line: a candidate with the lower average still gets a line right that the other misses. Both remain available. This command uses GEPA's per-example candidate sampling.

Question: why keep the lower-scoring candidate instead of always selecting the better one?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

Its different strength gives us another useful parent to improve. Here the dimensions are individual validation examples. The accuracy/cost frontier in the slides illustrates the broader idea of balancing multiple objectives.

</details>

Try a different `--seed` and compare the sampled parent. The [candidate-selection guide](https://gepa-ai.github.io/gepa/guides/candidate-selection/) explains the strategy.

## Reflective Prompt Mutation

_~12 min · Hands-on_

**Run a candidate → inspect feedback → propose an edit → check it.**

First, let's inspect the feedback from one failed training example:

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab feedback
```

```console
scoring with openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

candidate:
  Classify this log line as page, ticket, or ignore.
score: 0

line: CRITICAL staging db-primary replication halted, replica lag 1840s and climbing
expected: ignore
answered: page
feedback: Expected ignore, answered page. Staging never reaches on-call; the staging owners watch their own dashboard.

1 model calls
```

What change would help this example? Now let's run one refinement using recorded replies: the proposal and every score come from a run we recorded, so this step costs nothing. GEPA still performs the selection and acceptance checks.

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab evolve --fixtures --refinements 1 --out runs/reflection
```

```console

    - ticket: a person should look at it on the next working day, but nobody needs waking. Use this for degraded performance, slow jobs, recoverable or non-urgent errors that still warrant follow-up, and capacity or trend warnings.
    - ignore: no human action is needed. Use this for transient failures that self-recovered or were retried successfully, routine informational noise, and events already resolved.

    Rules:
    - Judge by business impact, not log level. An INFO line can require a page (for example, a storage policy exposing customer data). An ERROR line can be ignore (for example, a timeout that was retried and confirmed successful).
    - Anything involving money, payments, ledgers, or reconciliation discrepancies is at least page unless the line explicitly states it was resolved.
    - Anything involving customer data access, exposure, or permissions is page.

saved runs/reflection/run.json
```

Find the selected parent, four feedback examples, proposed prompt, and validation result in that order. Success! We've followed one complete refinement.

GEPA first compares the parent and proposal on the same training minibatch. An improvement earns evaluation on the larger validation set. An unsuccessful proposal is discarded.

## System-Aware Merge

_~10 min · Hands-on_

**Two useful branches → combine different improvements → check the result.**

For this exercise, we've split the prompt into two editable text components, like separate module prompts in a larger system:

- `definitions` improves the definitions component, which says what each label means.
- `rules` improves the rules component, which covers the lines a definition alone gets wrong.

Both descend from the same seed. Let's combine their separate changes; the merge itself needs no reflection call, only scoring:

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab merge
```

```console
scoring with openrouter/anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5

Common ancestor: seed
  definitions changed the definitions component
  rules changed the rules component

Same training minibatch:
  definitions   66.7%
  rules         66.7%
  merged        66.7%

No improvement on the minibatch; GEPA would discard this merge.

9 model calls
```

Compare both parents and the merged candidate on the same three lines. The merge only ties its parents, so GEPA discards it and never spends the 12 validation calls.

Question: each parent fixed a different line, so why didn't the merge fix both?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

The components interact. With the house rules in the same prompt, the model labelled the retried S3 upload `ticket`, a line `definitions` alone got right. Combining useful changes still needs evaluation. This prepared exercise follows the component-combination idea in [GEPA, Appendix D.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457); the single-prompt live run uses reflective mutation.

</details>

## Run the loop, one step at a time

_~5 min · Hands-on_

Let's use the sandbox model for up to **three refinements**, pausing after each. Press Enter to continue, or `q` to finish early. This is the one step that spends real money, so three is the cap.

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab evolve --refinements 3 --pause --out runs/live
```

At each pause, identify the parent, feedback, edit, and decision. Live proposals and scores will vary. A rejected proposal still uses one refinement.

The defaults use four examples per reflection, four scoring calls in flight, a 1,024-token output cap, and no automatic reflection retries. The 96-evaluation threshold caps scoring calls; `--refinements` caps proposal attempts.

<details>
<summary>Model choices</summary>

The sandbox uses its allowed model. Otherwise the lab's code chooses [Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite on OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite), [GPT-5.4 nano](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-nano), [Claude Haiku 4.5](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/haiku-4-5/overview), or [Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite), according to the available key.

Use `--model` to choose another LiteLLM model. Use a fresh `--out` directory for each run.

</details>

To continue without model calls, use this replay instead. It reuses recorded replies and scores; the selection and acceptance checks still run locally.

```bash
cd ~/zenable-labs/labs/gepa-prompt-evolution
uv run --locked python -m gepalab evolve --fixtures --refinements 3 --out runs/replay
```

```console
    You are triaging a single production log line for an on-call rotation. Reply with exactly one word: page, ticket, or ignore.

    Judge each line by its business impact on customers, money, data, and security, not by its log level or how alarming the wording sounds.

    Definitions:
    - page: someone must be woken now. Use this when a line shows an ongoing or unrecovered impact that will get worse or stay broken until a human acts: customer data exposure or privacy breach, payments or money integrity problems (any unreconciled or mismatched charge, however small, unless the line says it was resolved), security posture changes, active data loss, a user-facing outage that is ongoing, or a shared resource that is about to fail and will stall dependent services within minutes (for example, a queue or buffer nearing its memory limit so producers will block).
    - ticket: a person should look at it on the next working day, but nobody needs waking. Use this for degraded or slow performance that does not currently block customers, recoverable or non-urgent errors that still warrant follow-up, capacity or trend warnings with time to act, and planned changes or deprecations with a future deadline.
    - ignore: no human action is needed. Use this for transient failures that self-recovered or were retried and then succeeded, expected effects of routine operations (such as a rolling deploy taking instances out of rotation while healthy capacity remains), routine informational noise, and events already fully resolved.

    Rules:
    - An INFO line can require a page (for example, a storage policy exposing customer data). An ERROR line can be ignore (for example, a timeout that was retried and confirmed successful).
    - Anything involving money, payments, ledgers, or reconciliation discrepancies is at least page unless the line explicitly states it was resolved.
    - Anything involving customer data access, exposure, or permissions is page.
    - When a line indicates the problem is resolved, lean toward ignore unless the resolved issue was a payments or data-exposure event.
    - Before choosing ticket for an error or warning, ask whether the affected behavior is still happening right now or is a normal, expected part of an operation in progress. Expected operational churn is ignore; a real degradation without customer impact is ticket.
    - Before choosing ignore for a warning about a resource, ask whether it will exhaust within minutes and block other services. If so, it is page.
```

```console
     - page: someone must be woken now. Use this for anything that threatens customer data exposure or privacy, payments or money integrity (including any unreconciled or mismatched charge, however small), security posture changes, data loss, or a user-facing outage that is ongoing or unrecovered.
     - ticket: a person should look at it on the next working day, but nobody needs waking. Use this for degraded performance, slow jobs, recoverable or non-urgent errors that still warrant follow-up, and capacity or trend warnings.
     - ignore: no human action is needed. Use this for transient failures that self-recovered or were retried successfully, routine informational noise, and events already resolved.

     Rules:
     - Judge by business impact, not log level. An INFO line can require a page (for example, a storage policy exposing customer data). An ERROR line can be ignore (for example, a timeout that was retried and confirmed successful).
     - Anything involving money, payments, ledgers, or reconciliation discrepancies is at least page unless the line explicitly states it was resolved.
     - Anything involving customer data access, exposure, or permissions is page.
     - When a line indicates the problem is resolved, lean toward ignore unless the resolved issue was a payments or data-exposure event.
     - Use ticket for slow or degraded behavior that does not affect customers right now.

     Output only the single word: page, ticket, or ignore. No punctuation, no explanation.
```

Use `runs/live/run.json` to inspect your live run. Held-out lines weren't used to choose candidates. Eight held-out lines make this a small teaching example.

Before we finish, explain which candidate was selected, what feedback changed the text, and why a proposal was kept or discarded.
